chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked, 'Do I wipe over the two socks (al-khuffayn) out of precaution (taqiyyah)?' He said, 'Three things in which I do not fear anyone: drinking the intoxicant, wiping over the two socks, and Tamattu' al-Hajj.'

key_terms.الْخُفَّيْنِ: the two socks (leather foot coverings worn over socks)
key_terms.تَقِيَّةً: out of precaution (concealing belief to avoid harm)
key_terms.مَتْعَةُ الْحَجِّ: Tamattu' al-Hajj (a type of pilgrimage combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: Does the Imam wipe over his socks out of precaution or as a standard ruling?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Zurarah asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether wiping over the leather socks (*khuffayn*) is a practice of precaution (*taqiyyah*) or a firm ruling. The Imam responds that it is one of three practices he performs with confidence, not fearing criticism, alongside drinking wine (*al-muskir*) and performing *Tamattu' al-Hajj*. This indicates that wiping over the socks is a well-established practice in Shia jurisprudence, not merely a precautionary measure.
